A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGPO study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Shared content can be matched reliably despite additions, revisions, and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational experiments on TrpB and CreiLOV, including oracle validation, guided generation, adaptive optimization, and ensemble analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original computational experiments and adds GB1 evaluations and additional adaptive-optimization comparisons, including APEXGo.

M1.justification: The proposed discrete DAPS procedure, classifier guidance, and ensemble-based adaptive optimization in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The revised DPO loss concerns the comparison baseline; added benchmarks and preprocessing revisions do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds GB1 binding optimization across all 56 residues alongside TrpB enzyme activity and CreiLOV fluorescence (Table 2). This introduces another protein family and fitness objective, with evaluations spanning prior generation, steering, and adaptive optimization.

E2.justification: Figure 6 newly evaluates APEXGo and adds Continuous+NOS to the adaptive comparison, whereas NOS previously appeared only in single-round steering comparisons. Appendix A.4.4 also substantively revises the ARLM+DPO baseline from ranked to weighted loss.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces variable-length, gap-removed ARLM training fragments with gap-filled sequences and introduces mutations near sequence starts. Table A3 changes the DPO learning rate from 1e-4 to 1e-6 and selected beta from 2 to 0.1, and expands NOS parameter sweeps. GB1 and APEXGo also introduce additional training and evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The existing NOS sensitivity analysis expands to varying step size and iteration count as well as lambda. Appendix A.4.4 adds qualitative checks of DPO learning-rate failure and alternative loss performance. The ensemble-versus-single-model ablation remains unchanged in Table A4 and v1 Figure A6/v2 Figure A7.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten standardized steering datasets with standard-deviation error bars in Figure 5 and five random initializations for adaptive experiments and ensemble analyses. New results extend these practices without changing repeat counts or introducing new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive GB1 results, including oracle Pearson correlations of 0.89 for training, validation, and testing in Figure A1, plus new APEXGo and Continuous+NOS adaptive results. ARLM, DPO, and NOS results on retained tasks are also revised under changed settings, so they are not same-setting performance gains. Table A4's numerical entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 21 changes the formal DPO objective by adding fitness weights to the previously unweighted ranked-loss expression. The diffusion and guidance equations, DAPS approximation and convergence discussion, and adaptive algorithm otherwise remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims about effective low-label SGPO and ensemble-guided exploration remain. The introduction and Discussion now single out DAPS as strongest overall, replacing the earlier emphasis on CG and DAPS jointly, and add an explicit performance claim against latent-space Bayesian optimization with APEXGo.

C2.justification: The Discussion adds explanations involving APEXGo's trust-region calibration and latent-space geometry, and suggests selecting guidance strength using sample uniqueness and novelty. It removes the limitation that only proteins with many homologs were studied, while retaining qualifications concerning oracle generalization, native functions, and limited fitness labels.

D1.justification: v2 documents GB1 augmentation and oracle training, and adds APEXGo implementation details, training epochs, and acquisition budgets in Appendix A.6. ARLM preparation and steering hyperparameters are updated. The existing code-access information, architecture tables, and hardware discussion remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 and Table 1 substantially expand positioning relative to zero-shot design, adaptive search, GFlowNets, and latent-space optimization, including Jain et al. (2022) and Torres et al. (2024). Brookes et al. (2019) is reclassified from Generative: Adaptive to SGPO, and the claimed gap in prior adaptive optimization is softened. These are substantive changes beyond publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Discussion receive localized rewrites and clarifications. Affiliations, conference information, and acknowledgments expand, and a new APEXGo subsection precedes the appendix results. The main section sequence and most technical exposition are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and the novelty figure expand from six to nine panels, while Figure 6 changes from a two-by-two model/task grid to three dataset panels with revised legends. GB1 oracle and prior displays are added, Figure 3 gains a latent-optimization branch, and Tables 1–2 expand. The ensemble-diversity figure is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the comparison by addressing v1's acknowledged NOS/DPO tuning concerns, adding the relevant APEXGo baseline, and testing GB1 binding with a much smaller natural MSA. These changes improve the fairness and breadth of evidence supporting the central conclusions. The new GB1 training count in Table 2 is not clearly reconciled with Appendix A.2's split description, and oracle-generalization limitations persist, but these qualifications do not outweigh the stronger comparative evidence.
